text: Reputation governance must be revisable on the timescale of exploitation and able to ingest evidence of its own gaming.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Governance must also be revisable on the timescale of the exploit rather than the timescale of the standards cycle. The Folk Theorem result forecloses a static rule set. The author's dynamic-regulation framework supplies the alternative: rules are adaptable only where "the institutions and rulemaking processes that produce them integrate dynamic elements that generate timely, relevant, and decentralized information for rulemaking" (Kaal 2013, claim 2267560-012). A reputation protocol whose governance cannot ingest evidence of its own gaming is a reputation protocol with a fixed expiry date.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems
